newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar strengthens on budget projections.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar strengthens on budget projections.

text.p: * Canada's dollar firmed to C$1.3524 (US$0.7395) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3536 (US$0.7388), gathering most of its strength in heavy trading after a budget update from Canada's finance minister, dealers said.
* They said the budget projections were better than expected and should attract overseas and domestic buying.

The Canadian dollar ended firmer at C$1.3624 (US$0.7395) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3536 (US$0.7388), gathering most of its strength in heavy trading after a budget update from Canada's finance minister, dealers said.
Finance Minister Paul Martin said Canada's final budget deficit for fiscal 1995/96 was C$28.6 billion, down from a projected C$32,7 billion.
"It's a little bit rosier than we would have thought," said one dealer. "The (deficit) number is looking pretty solid, and the projections look reasonable."
The currency softened during morning trading as market players awaited Martin's announcement, dealers said.
But the day's weakness was quickly chased away with Martin's speech and the optimism about Canada's economy is expected to continue overnight with buying from Asia and Europe, dealers said.
"There's continued pressure on the currency to strengthen," said one dealer. "It's generally a good sentiment all around."
Dealers said the currency will likely bounce off the C$1.3500 (US$0.7407) level, however.
They said market players fear the Bank of Canada would move to lower short-term interest rates again if the Canadian dollar strengthens above that level.

The currency "has come a long way in Canada terms. Not too long ago we were at C$1.3700 and now we're down here near the year's low," said one dealer. "This is the appreciation we've been waiting for."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar eased to 1.1291 marks from Tuesday's close at 1.1298 marks and softened to 82.37 yen from 82.43 yen.
